elements.brief_element: End-to-end delivery sequence: a signed revision from a protected branch is built, tested, scanned, published immutably with provenance, promoted unchanged through staging after migration checks and tests, approved for production, canaried from 5% through 25%, 50%, and 100%, and automatically paused or rolled back when health cannot be established.
elements.brief_evidence: Across the brief: “protected branch produces a signed source revision”; “Successful builds publish an immutable image and provenance statement”; “promotes the same image into a staging environment”; “Production promotion requires an approved change record”; “send five percent of traffic”; “Healthy windows increase traffic to twenty-five, fifty, and one hundred percent”; and unavailable telemetry or breached thresholds cause pause or rollback.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction recovers the build, immutable publication, same-image staging promotion, approval, primary 5% canary, metric evaluation, 25% → 50% → 100% ramp, pause, and rollback. It then adds “Primary complete” followed by a mandatory “Secondary-region canary” with another independent ramp.
elements.note: The original delivery lifecycle is visible, but the reconstruction materially changes its production topology by inserting sequential primary- and secondary-region rollouts that the brief never defines.

unsupported_claims.claim: Production rollout is divided into a primary region followed by a secondary region.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The purpose says the image is canaried “first in a primary region and then independently in a secondary region,” and the components include sections “3A · Primary-region canary” and “3B · Secondary-region canary.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief specifies one production canary rollout and names no regions or sequential regional deployment topology.

unsupported_claims.claim: The secondary-region canary begins only after the primary region reaches 100%, using the same revision.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: “Primary complete” says “Begin the secondary canary with the same immutable revision,” and its output is labeled “primary complete · same revision.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief does not define a second canary, a regional ordering constraint, or a primary-to-secondary handoff.

unsupported_claims.claim: A separate secondary canary controller starts another 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% rollout with independent observation windows.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: Components include “Secondary canary controller,” secondary “5% traffic,” “Independent observation windows,” and “Secondary ramp 25% → 50% → 100%.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Only one canary controller and one sequence of consecutive observation windows and traffic increments are described.

unsupported_claims.claim: Ordinary secondary-region failures roll back only the secondary region.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The failure path routes a secondary failure through “Freeze secondary rollout” to “Rollback secondary region only,” and the “Failure scope” note states that a secondary failure is isolated to that region.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief has no regional failure-isolation policy; its breached-threshold outcome is rollback to the last known-good image.

unsupported_claims.claim: A shared business-metric breach during the secondary rollout rolls back both regions.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The “Shared business...” yes-branch reaches “Rollback both regions to last known-good image,” and the failure-scope note says only a shared business-metric breach triggers rollback in both regions.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief includes a business success metric among canary metrics but does not define shared-versus-regional breaches or a special two-region rollback rule.

unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction contains an “Append-only evidence” component and states that audit evidence is append-only.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires the listed events to enter an audit log but does not state an append-only storage guarantee.

unsupported_claims.claim: A healthy staging result creates or records the approved change record.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The green branch from “Staging healthy?” is described as creating an “Approved change record,” which then enables canary promotion.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says production promotion requires an approved change record; it does not say staging health creates or approves that record.

unsupported_claims.claim: Image-signature verification specifically occurs between selection of the same image and the database compatibility check in staging.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The staging flow orders “Same immutable image,” “Verify its signature,” and then “DB compati...”.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires that signature verification cannot be bypassed but does not locate that verification specifically within this staging sequence.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The central canary safety loop is transmitted very well: approved promotion starts at 5%, evaluates error rate, latency, saturation, and business success over consecutive windows, ramps through 25%, 50%, and 100% when healthy, pauses on missing telemetry, and freezes and rolls back to the last known-good image on a breached threshold.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: The board introduces an unsupported mandatory primary-then-secondary regional rollout with independent second canary evaluation and region-scoped rollback rules. This changes the production architecture and failure semantics enough that engineers could implement a materially different system from the one in the brief.
verdict.overall_summary: Most stated build, staging, canary, audit, notification, and operator-control behaviors are individually recoverable, including the same immutable artifact, gate failures, staging preservation, metric set, traffic ramp, telemetry pause, automatic rollback, and non-bypass constraints. Important details are softened around registry publication, approval ownership, active-revision agreement, and migration-controller compensation safety. More seriously, the reconstruction adds a second regional rollout and new rollback-scoping policy, contradicting the brief's single canary operational story. The main happy path remains recognizable, but the invented regional topology would lead to a materially different production design.
